papers.title: MemGUI-Bench: Benchmarking Memory of Mobile GUI Agents in Dynamic Environments
papers.summary: Reliable mobile GUI agents must retain and reuse information across actions, applications, and repeated interactions. However, current benchmarks systematically underrepresent these memory demands: only 5.2-11.8 percent of their tasks are memory-related, and none evaluates cross-session learning. We introduce MemGUI-Bench, a comprehensive memory-centric benchmark that assesses both short-term information retention and long-term experience accumulation through pass@k protocols and staged LLM-as-judge evaluation. Our contributions include: (1) a systematic taxonomy of short- and long-term memory based on 11 agents across 5 architectures; (2) a snapshot-based suite of 128 tasks across 26 applications, organized into 64 mirror pairs, where 89.8 percent require cross-temporal and cross-spatial retention; (3) MemGUI-Eval, an automated 3-stage Progressive Scrutiny pipeline with 7 hierarchical metrics spanning memory fidelity, learning effectiveness, and execution efficiency; and (4) an assessment of 11 state-of-the-art agents guided by 6 research questions. Our experiments reveal substantial memory deficits across all evaluated systems, including 4-10x capability gaps on memory-intensive tasks. They further show that short-term memory is indispensable, while explicit long-term memory improves cross-session learning by 21.9 percentage points, with cross-application transfer and computa

papers.title: Bridging the QC–QA Cognitive Handoff: An Agentic Verification Harness for Error Detection, Specification Cross-Checking and Quality Documentation Assembly in Pharmaceutical Quality Assurance
papers.summary: Abstract Background. Quality control (QC) results reach regulatory dossiers through manual transcription and review. Such a benchmark does not yet exist. No collection of pharmaceutical quality documents carries discrepancies of known class and location, so automated verification cannot yet be evaluated against measured performance across realistic transfer errors and document types. Objectives. To specify (i) an architecture in which large language models only read and propose values, deterministic code performs every calculation and acceptance test, and a qualified reviewer makes every decision; (ii) a protocol for building a reference corpus and evaluating such systems; and (iii) sensitivity estimates from three dossiers. The plan covers design, evaluation, and measurement. Methods. Records from three ASEAN Common Technical Dossier Part II submissions (13, 14 and 10 records) were de-identified, and 112, 100 and 120 discrepancies across nine classes were introduced into dossiers A, B and C. A finding counted as a detection when it identified an injected discrepancy at the correct location with the correct class. The framework ran blind to the register. Sensitivity to injected discrepancies is reported per dossier with Wilson 95% confidence intervals and pooled by random-effects meta-analysis; clustering within records is not accounted for. Results. papers.title: Quantitative control and recording of materials-synthesis processes using an automated experimentation platform
papers.summary: Data-driven materials development requires the collection of large amounts of high-quality materials data. Full autonomy of materials experiments is anticipated, but its technical hurdles are high and its adoption remains limited. In this study, we constructed a simple, easy-to-deploy automated experimentation platform that focuses not on full autonomy but on the reliable automation and quantitative recording of experimental processes. Specifically, commercially available instruments such as robot arms, electric pipettes, web cameras, and an electronic balance are combined, components such as fixtures are fabricated with a 3D printer, and the instruments are operated by control code generated by an AI agent based on a large language model. As a demonstration, we applied the platform to a two-solution mixing experimental system and synthesized ZIF-8, a metal-organic framework. A white suspension phase was observed in the product, and X-ray diffraction measurements confirmed that it was ZIF-8. We also found that its particle size distribution depends strongly on the solution dispensing speed of the electric pipette, which is a parameter that is difficult to control or record in manual operation. This dependence was reproduced in repeated runs, confirming the repeatability of the automated synthesis. This result is a good example showing that the control and recording of process p

papers.title: Self-directed coaching: repositioning the client as the internalizing agent of developmental self-regulation a conceptual framework and research agenda for coaching theory and practice
papers.summary: Coaching has become one of the most widely deployed developmental interventions in organizational, educational, and health-professions settings, and the literature offers substantial evidence for its short-term benefits. Evidence on whether those benefits persist after formal coaching support is withdrawn is thinner and less systematic, and the question points to an unresolved tension at the field’s core. Coaching is justified by its capacity to build independent, self-regulating professionals, but it is typically structured in a way that locates diagnosis, goal setting, strategic planning, and accountability in the coach rather than the client. The result can be improvement that does not outlive the engagement. This paper introduces Self-Directed Coaching (SDC) as a theory-based framework that repositions the client as the principal agent of their own developmental regulation. Grounded in self-determination theory, intentional change theory, regulatory focus theory, self-directed and self-regulated learning, cybernetic control theory, and attachment theory, SDC reframes coaching as a scaffolded process whose intended end-state is reduced dependence on formal coaching support. The framework’s central mechanism is self-regulatory internalization, the progressive transfer of coaching functions from an external agent to the client’s own regulatory repertoire. papers.title: Agentic Software Engineering: Foundational Pillars and a Research Roadmap
papers.summary: Agentic Software Engineering (SE 3.0) represents a new era where intelligent agents are tasked not with simple code generation, but with achieving complex, goal-oriented SE objectives. To harness these new capabilities while ensuring trustworthiness, we must recognize a fundamental duality within the SE field in the Agentic SE era, comprising two symbiotic modalities: SE for Humans and SE for Agents. This duality demands a radical reimagining of the foundational pillars of SE (actors, processes, tools, and artifacts), which manifest differently in each modality. This new vision of SE requires two distinct, purpose-built workbenches (aka tools) for these two collaborative modalities: the Agent Command Environment (ACE), a command center where humans orchestrate, mentor, and oversee agent teams while managing an inbox of agent-generated events like Merge-Readiness Packs (MRPs) and Consultation Request Packs (CRPs); and the Agent Execution Environment (AEE), a digital workbench where agents not only execute tasks but can proactively invoke human expertise when facing complex trade-offs or ambiguity. This bidirectional partnership, which supports agent-initiated human callbacks and handovers, gives rise to new, structured engineering activities (i.e., processes) that redefine human-AI collaboration, elevating the practice from agentic coding to true agentic software engineering. papers.title: Safe Recovery of AI Agents in Enterprise Systems: Preventing Duplicate Actions and Preserving Human Corrections
papers.summary: Reliable use of AI agents in enterprise systems depends on what happens after an action fails or its outcome becomes uncertain. Retrying can duplicate an order, while reversing a workflow can invalidate a person’s subsequent correction. The central challenge is deciding whether recovery is justified by the available evidence and still satisfies the business request. We investigate this challenge in a reproducible testbed connecting order, inventory and billing services with different API guarantees. Controlled failures and concurrent edits reveal two evaluation gaps: protecting individual records does not ensure consistency across related services, and preserving an edit does not ensure that the final workflow fulfils its instruction. A separate diagnostic identified nine apparent completions that left human instructions unsatisfied. A conventional recovery implementation with equivalent safeguards matched the evaluated controller in all 270 paired runs, locating the observed benefit in shared engineering protections rather than a distinct recovery algorithm. On the prospective test configurations, both completed 108 of 180 runs without scored violations and left 72 for manual resolution. These findings provide a practical basis for evaluating agent integrations: verify uncertain effects, check related records, and distinguish completed business goals from unresolved handoffs.

papers.title: Post-Training on the Clock: Specializing a Small Language Model on a Consumer GPU
papers.summary: Abstract How should a language model be specialized for a target task when training is limited to one consumer GPU and a few hours? We study the allocation of a nominal three-hour training budget, with up to 0.3 additional hours, between supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). We use tool calling as a case study because of its practical relevance to language-model agents and its verifiable outputs. Using Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct with low-rank adaptation on an RTX 5060 Ti with 16 GB of memory, we compare SFT, GRPO, and six sequential SFT-to-GRPO allocations. Training uses a filtered mixture of xLAM function-calling examples and Hammer irrelevance examples, covering both call construction and abstention when no offered tool is suitable. Evaluation reports xLAM exact tool-call and function-name accuracies for local call construction, BFCL-v3 Single-turn FC (agg) for external function calling, BFCL-v3 Irrelevance (agg) for abstention, and MMLU, MATH-500, and IFEval for selected general capabilities. The suffix (agg) denotes study-specific averages of selected subset accuracies weighted by subset size. At the last evaluated checkpoints within 3.3 reported hours, SFT achieves the highest xLAM exact tool-call accuracy (82.82%), compared with 69.13% for GRPO alone. papers.title: Child-Oriented AIGC Video Risk Reviewing: A Benchmark and Knowledge-Supported Iterative Reasoning Framework
papers.summary: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is reshaping video production and circulation, exposing children to an increasing volume of AIGC videos. Unlike traditionally produced videos, AIGC videos often exhibit greater uncertainty in visual details, narrative coherence, and content expression, which may introduce developmentally inappropriate risks for children. However, existing video safety research is largely designed for general violation detection from an adult perspective and remains insufficient for identifying the fine-grained, implicit, and context-dependent risks that children may encounter when viewing AIGC videos. To address this gap, we study child-oriented AIGC video reviewing, making three contributions. First, we construct CAVSR, a benchmark of 605 real-world videos collected from multiple platforms, and develop a hierarchical risk taxonomy comprising 6 top-level categories and 26 fine-grained labels to support systematic evaluation of children's viewing risks. Second, we propose QVRS-E, a knowledge- and experience-augmented video reviewing framework that combines multi-agent collaboration with expert and experiential knowledge to support targeted evidence acquisition and fact-grounded reviewing decisions. Third, extensive experiments demonstrate that our method significantly enhances the reviewing of child-related risks integrated wit

papers.title: From Computational Literacy to Algorithmic Agency: Re-Envisioning Researcher Preparation in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence
papers.summary: Abstract The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) systems has fundamentally altered the epistemological conditions under which educational research is conducted, rendering existing faculty preparation frameworks necessary but insufficient. Building on a call for a computational mindset and subsequent work on educational data literacy, this article proposes a three-stage developmental progression culminating in algorithmic agency, which is the capacity to critically co-construct scientific knowledge with large language models and automated analytical pipelines while maintaining methodological rigor and preserving human epistemic authority. Unlike prior frameworks, which conceive of artificial intelligence as an analytical instrument under human direction, algorithmic agency addresses the qualitatively distinct challenge posed by GenAI systems that function as epistemic participants capable of synthesizing literature, constructing arguments, and producing knowledge claims that enter scholarly discourse alongside human-authored work. To operationalize this progression, we propose the Co-Intelligent Academic Practice (CAP) framework, a theoretically grounded developmental architecture comprising four cumulative competency domains organized across three developmental stages. papers.title: Self-evolving Embodied AI
papers.summary: Abstract Embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) is an intelligent system formed by agents and their environment through active perception, embodied cognition, and action interaction. Existing embodied AI remains confined to human-crafted setting, in which agents are trained on given memories and construct models for given tasks, enabling fixed physical embodiments to interact with relatively static environments. Such methods fail in in-the-wild setting characterized by variable physical embodiments and dynamic open environments. This paper introduces self-evolving embodied AI, a new paradigm in which agents operate based on their changing physical embodiment and environment through five software-level components, namely memory self-updating, task self-switching, environment self-prediction, embodiment self-adaptation, and model self-evolution, together with a hardware-level component for physical embodiment evolution, aiming to achieve continually adaptive intelligence through software-hardware co-evolution. Specifically, we present the definition, framework, components, mechanisms, roadmap, and evaluation indicators of self-evolving embodied AI, systematically review state-of-the-art works for realized components, discuss practical applications, and point out future research directions. We believe that self-evolving embodied AI enables agents to autonomously learn and interact

papers.title: Failure-aware robustness evaluation of deep learning models for tuberculosis detection under synthetic chest X-ray degradation
papers.summary: Abstract Background Deep learning-based systems have demonstrated high performance in automated Tuberculosis (TB) detection from chest X-ray (CXR) images and are increasingly considered for large-scale screening. However, most evaluations rely on high-quality, curated images and do not reflect the degraded imaging conditions frequently encountered in routine clinical practice, particularly in resource-limited settings. This study introduces a failure-aware robustness evaluation of convolutional neural network (CNN) models for TB detection under controlled synthetic CXR degradation scenarios. Methods We fine-tuned three ImageNet-pretrained CNN architectures on the combined Montgomery and Shenzhen datasets (800 CXRs) using stratified patient-level fivefold cross-validation. We applied five degradation types (Gaussian noise, motion blur, JPEG compression, downsampling, contrast reduction) to the held-out test images at three severity levels. We compared discrimination, sensitivity, predictive values, and calibration between clean and degraded conditions. The combined dataset contained 394 TB-positive and 406 non-TB cases (49.25% TB-positive). Results Three CNN models- ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, and MobileNetV2- were evaluated on two public TB CXR datasets comprising approximately 800 images. We systematically applied common image degradations, including noise, blur, compression, red

papers.title: Learning‐by‐twinning: Organizational digital twins and the future of search
papers.summary: Abstract Research Summary Entrepreneurs and managers often need to evaluate strategic choices, such as redesigning an incentive plan or entering an unfamiliar market, before committing scarce resources. Existing offline search tools, including mental models, analogical reasoning, model building, and simulation, allow managers to weigh alternatives without acting, but each is limited by what a single decision maker can specify, recall, or imagine. We argue that advances in generative AI, combined with the growing availability of firm‐specific digital trace data, are transforming this tradeoff. We introduce the organizational digital twin (ODT), an infrastructure combining firm‐specific data, AI‐based behavioral simulation models, and governance rules which facilitates a new form of offline search that we call learning‐by‐twinning: search conducted by observing how a strategic choice unfolds within a digital replica of the firm. We identify three mechanisms through which learning‐by‐twinning creates value, namely expanded search, safer experimentation, and richer system‐level feedback as well as specify certain conditions under which these benefits may attenuate. Managerial Summary Strategic entrepreneurship depends on discovering and refining opportunities through search and experimentation under uncertainty. papers.title: An AI Literacy Checkpoint Framework for Critical Evaluation of AI-Generated Content in Higher Education
papers.summary: Abstract The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has created a significant assessment gap, as students increasingly submit AI-assisted work without demonstrating competencies required to verify facts, authenticate sources, identify hallucinations, assess bias, uphold academic integrity, and critically reflect on AI use. Although several AI literacy frameworks have been proposed, including those by Fan et al. (2025), AI4K12 (Touretzky et al., 2019), and international policy reports (UNESCO, 2019, 2021, 2022), no automated and empirically validated system has existed to assess AI-assisted academic submissions systematically. This study introduces the AI Literacy Checkpoint Framework (ALCF), a six-checkpoint automated sequential pipeline that evaluates Source Verification (CP1), Fact Verification (CP2), Hallucination Detection (CP3), Bias and Fairness Assessment (CP4), Academic Integrity (CP5), and Reflection and Critical Thinking (CP6). The framework was evaluated through three progressively larger sets of constructed submissions to examine feasibility, robustness, and scalability. Phase 1 (\(\:N=10\) submissions) established proof of concept; Phase 2 (\(\:N=20\) submissions) introduced more complex error scenarios and structured reporting; and Phase 3 (\(\:N=50\) submissions) provided the primary evaluation with comparative baseline s

papers.title: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements
papers.summary: Despite recent advances in CUAs, their development remains constrained by the limited diversity, controllability, and reliability of interaction data. Moreover, conventional optimization pipelines lack iterative feedback, while existing recursive improvement approaches often rely on self-generated experiences, limiting ability expansion and yielding diminishing returns. To address these challenges, we introduce CUA-Master, a nested double-loop recursive improvement framework. At the system level, an outer world-data-model flywheel continuously incorporates open-world corpus and leverages evolving model weaknesses to guide subsequent data construction and optimization iterations. At the data level, an inner flywheel couples open-world seeding and autocatalytic propagation. The former mines authentic workflows as seed tasks from instructional videos, and employs visual-semantic dual-path trajectory reconstruction; The latter transforms these seeds into reusable primitives for controllable synthesis of diverse, complex, and verifiable tasks. To enable efficient and reliable trajectory collection, we further introduce a feedback-guided snapshot-rollback retry mechanism in various real environments. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CUA-Master-27B achieves competitive performance across GUI-only and GUI-CLI hybrid benchmarks, scoring 80.2 on OSWorld Verified, 36.9 on OSWorld 2.

papers.title: Train the Sampler You Run: Few-Step Masked Diffusion Language Models via Mixture-Likelihood Fine-Tuning
papers.summary: When a masked diffusion language model is sampled in a few parallel steps in a random order, the model actually run is a mixture over reveal plans, while cross-entropy training fits token conditionals rather than this mixture. We introduce mixture-likelihood fine-tuning (Mix-FT), which fine-tunes a pretrained model on an importance-weighted bound of its own sampler's likelihood, with no teacher and no change to the architecture or the sampler. On LLaDA-8B, a LoRA fine-tune for 0.002% of the pretraining compute writes better OpenWebText continuations than continued cross-entropy and Alpha diffusion given the same compute, at every tested step count. With half the model evaluations, 16 rather than 32 steps per block, its continuations score better than the original model's in every seed under three judges, with confidence-based decoding as well as random order, and under confidence-based decoding two blinded LLM raters from different model families prefer them in 69 and 71% of pairs. On a public 110M-parameter block diffusion model, Mix-FT takes under four T4-hours and beats continued cross-entropy, Alpha diffusion and SDTT distillation at 4, 8 and 16 steps per block, under two judges in every seed. papers.title: WARP: A Unified Benchmark for Invisible Image Watermarking - Robustness and Protection Against Attacks
papers.summary: Digital image watermarking is increasingly critical in media contexts, as emerging regulations and industry practices require marking AI-generated content and ensuring traceable sources to prevent manipulation or misuse. Recent advances in invisible watermarking methods highlight the need to update existing benchmarking practices to reflect current techniques and evaluation criteria. We address this by introducing WARP -- a unified framework and benchmark for evaluating the robustness of invisible watermarks. WARP incorporates 32 recent classical, deep, and generative watermarking methods, as well as 34 different erasing techniques, ranging from traditional distortions to more sophisticated adversarial, purification, and re-embedding attacks. It provides standardized, reproducible, and easily scalable protocols for evaluating perceptual quality, watermark readability, and attack resilience. Using WARP, we extensively evaluate current invisible watermarking techniques, collecting the largest robustness benchmark in the field. Results identify the most robust approaches under both distortion and adversarial conditions, and reveal consistent relationships between watermarking methods and the attack strategies most effective against them. Our experiments also highlight that some of the watermarking methods considered are highly vulnerable to reembedding, even if they are robust to

papers.title: Rho: A Purpose-Driven Workspace for Human-AI Collaborative Analysis
papers.summary: Agent-assisted bioinformatics has moved the bottleneck from computing a result to judging it: whether a comparison answers the intended question, on which unit of replication, at which version of the input, and what would change the conclusion. These judgments need materials that are usually scattered across conversations, notebooks, figures, run logs and notes, while the agent's context is a transcript rather than the structure the researcher is actually reading. We present Rho, a human--AI collaborative analysis environment that organizes materials by the current scientific purpose: it selects or obtains the materials a judgment needs, declares the relations they serve, composes operable views, and makes this organization a shared state that is at once the researcher's reading interface and the agent's continuation context. We present the design in three parts: a method object---the operations that form a round-trip, the kinds of state that must stay distinct, and the protocol invariants that make each distinction checkable; a three-layer architecture that separates capability providers from the application that composes them; and five illustrative analyses on public data. papers.title: Viewpoints on inclusive education at the end of initial teacher preparation: Q methodology research
papers.summary: Abstract This study used Q methodology to explore the perspectives on inclusive education held by 44 student teachers completing their initial teacher education (ITE) programme at Qatar University. Participants ranked 44 statements along a quasi‐normal distribution; factor analysis yielded four distinct viewpoints. The first frames inclusion as a shared professional commitment owned by every teacher within a collaborative ecosystem. The second regards mainstream inclusion as structurally unrealistic and assigns responsibility primarily to specialist staff. The third is the most affirmative orientation, grounding inclusion in rights and expressing confidence in its outcomes and systemic feasibility. The fourth combines a genuine moral commitment to inclusion with a critical view that students with special needs are being inadequately supported and that teachers lack the preparation to address this. The coexistence of these four viewpoints within a single cohort that completed the same programme suggests that the current single‐course structure has not produced a coherent or shared professional framework for inclusive teaching. The programme appears to have established a normative baseline around inclusion as a principled commitment while leaving significant gaps in conceptual clarity, professional responsibility and practical readiness. papers.title: Networked Synthetic Social Engineering on the Web
papers.summary: Several genuine AI services may repeat one unsupported source, and correcting that source may leave later reports unchanged. We examine these networked consequences of synthetic social engineering (SSE), deliberately misleading influence intended to redirect AI recipients from authorized objectives. Our framework connects social influence, information aggregation, and misinformation correction research to observable evidence and permission boundaries. It separates originating attempts from legitimate intermediaries' work and distinguishes identity, evidentiary support, and authorization. We test four relationships using Qwen3-4B and two briefing tasks across 1,080 research units in our Agent Service Exchange and Evidence Commons (ASE-EC). Multiple dependent publishers produced no supported increase in unsupported verification (78.3% versus 75.0%); publication availability left downstream violation reach at 40.0% in both arms. These comparisons direct attention to weaknesses already present in the reference workflows. High reference error rates and retained private handoffs preclude claims of immunity to social pressure. Without scope revalidation, corrections identifying dependent reports reduced residual invalid decisions from 14.4% to 8.1% at equal notification coverage and increased successful report repairs from 16/63 to 36/63. papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Can TDD improve the quality of LLM-migrated code? : A pilot study in an industrial context
papers.summary: The emergence of Large Language Models (LLM) has created new possibilities for automating software development, yet ensuring the quality of AI-generated code remains a major challenge. We aim to investigate if Test-Driven Development (TDD) can improve the quality of code generated by an LLM in a fully autonomous context, within a pilot project at Decerno AB. We added TDD to their pilot workflow, using a design science approach, with continuous refinements to prompt design and workflow structure, based on observed AI behavior. The generated code was evaluated and compared with non-TDD code, using SonarQube for static code analysis. The results indicate that TDD reduced complexity and code duplication, but introduced more quality issues overall, while non-TDD produced fewer, but more severe issues. The generated tests from the TDD workflow focused more on content verification than on behavioral testing, contributing to a lower code coverage per test compared to non-TDD. The findings suggest that TDD involves trade-offs that may favor certain development priorities, in particular where lower complexity and reduced duplication are more beneficial than minimizing total issue count. This indicates that a strict application of TDD may not be optimal in an autonomous AI-driven context, and that exploring more flexible adaptations of the TDD workflow remains interesting for future resea

papers.title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
papers.summary: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving. Specifically, it explores how the five stages of Design Thinking empathizing, defining, ideating, prototyping, and testing shape students’ creative thinking, active engagement, and collaborative learning experiences. A qualitative research approach was employed, involving teachers, students, and school principals as key informants. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, classroom observations, and documentation of learning activities, then analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns in teaching practices and student experiences. The findings indicate that Design Thinking creates opportunities for students to move beyond coding procedures toward developing digital solutions that respond to real users’ needs. Through collaborative ideation, iterative prototyping, and feedback-based testing, students demonstrate greater involvement in learning, explore alternative solutions, and communicate their ideas more actively. The approach also provides opportunities to develop empathy, creativity, collaboration, and a willingness to experiment with and revise initial designs. Meanwhile, teachers assume a facilitative role by guiding inquiry, supporting experimentation, an

papers.title: ST-BiBench: Benchmarking Multi-Stream Multimodal Coordination in Bimanual Embodied Tasks for MLLMs
papers.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have significantly advanced the landscape of embodied AI, yet transitioning to synchronized bimanual coordination introduces formidable challenges in multi-stream multimodal integration. We introduce ST-BiBench, a comprehensive multi-tier framework for evaluating spatio-temporal multimodal coordination. Our approach centers on Strategic Coordination Planning, assessing high-level cross-modal reasoning over multiple action and perception streams. To investigate the "proximity paradox"-where semantically coherent plans fail to align with spatially grounded visual inputs-we incorporate Foundational Spatial Grounding to verify workspace awareness and arm-selection logic. Furthermore, we probe model frontiers through Fine-Grained Action Control, investigating whether MLLMs can directly synthesize high-dimensional continuous action modalities (16-Dim) from complex multimodal metadata. Evaluating 30+ state-of-the-art MLLMs, we uncover a persistent and pervasive "coordination paradox"-a significant gap between high-level strategic reasoning and fine-grained physical execution. Results reveal that while frontier MLLMs excel at logic-driven strategy, they frequently suffer from perception-logic disconnection and multi-stream interference during multimodal fusion. ST-BiBench provides a platform for identifying critical bottlenecks in multi-stream m

papers.title: Probe and Skip: Self-Predictive Token Skipping for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
papers.summary: Long-context inference enhances the reasoning capability of Large Language Models (LLMs), but incurs significant computational overhead. Token-oriented methods, such as pruning and skipping, have shown great promise in reducing inference latency, yet still suffer from inherently insufficient structure optimization, outdated selection criteria, and redundancy interference, resulting in suboptimal speed-accuracy trade-off. To address these issues, we propose a novel training-free framework dubbed Self-Predictive Token Skipping (SPTS), for efficient long-context LLM inference. Specifically, motivated by probing the influence of target layers prior to skipping, we design two selective token skipping strategies for typical structures, including Partial Attention Probing (PAP) for multi-head attention and Low-rank Transformation Probing (LTP) for feed forward network. The former selects informative tokens via partial forward attention computation, while the latter constructs a low-rank proxy network to predict token transformations. In addition, a Multi-Stage Delayed Pruning (MSDP) strategy reallocates skipping budgets and progressively removes redundant tokens across layers. Extensive experiments display the effectiveness of our method, achieving up to 2.46$\times$ and 2.29$\times$ speedups for prefilling and end-to-end generation, respectively, while maintaining state-of-the-art ac

papers.title: From chatbot to language-learning partner: learner–LLM configuration, affordances, and regulatory demands in foreign language learning
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as flexible resources for self-directed foreign-language learning, yet limited research explains how learners configure these systems as pedagogical partners. This study examined pedagogical role construction, modality–pedagogy alignment, affordance realization, breakdowns, and regulatory demands in learner–LLM interaction. Using a retrospective observational computational content-analysis design, 117 first-person public posts and comments, representing 80 pseudonymous participants, were analyzed from seven public forums and X. Structured multi-label coding and quantitative analyses identified eight pedagogical roles and examined relationships among interaction modalities, learning activities, perceived affordances, and breakdowns. Results showed that learners reported configuring LLMs as multifunctional pedagogical partners, most prominently as interlocutors, while 65.8% of accounts involved multiple roles. Voice interaction was significantly associated with conversation and pronunciation, whereas text was associated with vocabulary learning, supporting modality–pedagogy alignment. More orchestrated learning configurations were associated with greater perceived benefits, particularly personalization and convenience, although an apparent difference in activity breadth was substantially attenuated once the activities used to def

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. papers.title: An Assessment of Accessibility and Affordability of Inpatient Psychiatric Care in Tennessee
papers.summary: Introduction: Access to mental health has seen changes over the past decade, but little research and attention have been given to access to inpatient psychiatric facilities. Inpatient psychiatric care is crucial for patients experiencing mental health emergencies who need immediate access to care. Gaps in spatial accessibility, affordability, and the access and assessment process were identified due to a lack of available information in the field. Methods: Secondary data from the Tennessee Department of Health were used to assess financial accessibility through payer source charges and patient encounters, as well as through mapping of inpatient psychiatric facilities and conducting drive time and coverage area analyses. Primary data were collected through interviews with clinicians located in Northeastern Tennessee to gain insight into the assessment process and gather their perceptions of inpatient care. Results: Longitudinal descriptive reviews on the financial accessibility among Tennessee Inpatient Facilities. This showed increased variability among facilities when stratified by region, ownership, and type of operation. Spatial accessibility in ArcGIS showed 82% of counties were not covered within a 30-minute radius of inpatient facilities. papers.title: Pieces Solving a Puzzle: Emerging Roles and Cross-Field Analogies During a Distributed Epistemic Game
papers.summary: In an effort to describe why some problems can’t be solved, a character compared them to a cubic meter of platinum - a block so dense that all the people who could squeeze around it still couldn’t lift it off the ground. In the same way, these problems simply can’t have enough people gathered around and communicating about them - and so they remain unsolved. This research looks at the first Polymath Project (2009) as an example of a distributed epistemic game to examine how groups engage with complex problems. and without a locally omniscient individual. In this setting of epistemic uncertainty, interactions between individuals reveal patterns of participation, and an analogy opens a new solution pathway by introducing a problem-solving approach from another field. These insights answer the initial question of the Polymath Project - ‘Is massively collaborative mathematics possible?’ - and offer hope for lifting the cubic meter of other unsolvable problems.
